name: Coldwall Meridian Pocket Tee
description:
A midweight cotton-analog crew neck t-shirt in washed slate grey, cut slightly longer in the back with a single chest pocket bearing a small embossed Coldwall logo in matte black. The fabric has a lived-in texture from the first wear — soft but not fragile, with reinforced shoulder seams that hold their shape wash after wash. It's the kind of shirt you buy at a kiosk in a transit hub and end up wearing three times a week for two years.

Available in six muted colorways — slate, off-white, deep rust, olive, black, and a dusty mauve that sells out immediately. No tech, no features, no gimmicks. Just a very good t-shirt at a price that doesn't hurt.
what_it_says: You know what fits, you don't need to prove anything, and you've probably owned three of these in a row.
worn_by: anyone who just needs a shirt
story_hooks: A character finds a Coldwall tee in the exact colorway their dead sibling used to wear — same faded rust, same worn pocket corner.

Coldwall has been running a quiet recall on a specific production batch; the dye lot contains a trace compound that causes mild photosensitivity under UV-heavy lighting. Nobody's announced it officially.

A street fence is selling counterfeit Coldwall tees that are somehow better quality than the real thing — softer, better cut, and stamped with a serial number that doesn't exist in Coldwall's database.
